findings.title: JSON fix mode can emit prose/prompts or no JSON at all
findings.description: `opts.json` is only consulted after `runRoutedFix` returns, at `packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts:200-205`, but `runRoutedFix` does not receive `json`. In all-slices fix mode, `packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts:257-260` prints human text and returns `null` when there are no fixable findings, and `packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts:262-278` prints the dry-run report/plan and calls `askConfirmation` before applying fixes. `askConfirmation` writes the prompt to stdout (`packages/cli/src/utils/confirm.ts#askConfirmation`), so `cf check --fix --json` without `--yes` can produce prose plus a prompt followed by JSON, or no JSON on EOF/decline; `cf check --fix --yes --json` with no fixable findings also returns no JSON. The new integration cases at `packages/cli/tests/commands/check-worktree-fix.test.ts:190-249` cover `--yes`, single-slice, and `auto_fix` JSON paths, but not these explicit JSON paths. Pass JSON mode into `runRoutedFix` (or suppress preview/no-fix output there), fail cleanly or require `--yes` for non-interactive confirmations, and add tests that assert stdout is valid JSON for every `--json --fix` path.

findings.title: `extractFileIndex` breaks worktree ownership on Windows paths
findings.description: `ConsistencyChecker.extractFileIndex` uses `filePath.split('/').pop()` and `^(\d+)-` to derive `fixAction.subjectIndex`. The new aggregate/schema fix sites at `packages/core/src/introspection/ConsistencyChecker.ts:803`, `:871`, `:910`, `:968`, `:1068`, and `:1244` depend on this value. On Windows, paths built with `join()` use `\`, so the split returns the whole absolute path, the leading-index regex fails, and `subjectIndex` becomes `null`. `resolveFixOwner` (`packages/core/src/introspection/fixOwnership.ts#resolveFixOwner`) intentionally treats `null` as primary-checkout ownership, so plan/architecture/initiative/frontmatter-schema fixes can be routed to the wrong checkout or deferred as `NOT_OWNER`. Use `basename()` from `node:path` or split on both separators, and add a Windows-style path test instead of relying on POSIX-only fixtures.

findings.title: Readiness probes swallow timeout and unexpected git errors
findings.description: The blanket catch at `packages/core/src/git/checkoutReadiness.ts:41-46` converts any `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` failure into `NOT_A_CHECKOUT`, and the blanket catch at `packages/core/src/git/checkoutReadiness.ts:49-54` converts any `git symbolic-ref -q HEAD` failure into `DETACHED_HEAD`. `gateByReadiness` passes `FIX_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS` into these calls (`packages/core/src/introspection/routedFixes.ts:109-115`), so a timeout, lock error, or other unexpected `gitExec` failure is silently reported as a misleading deferral rather than logged/rethrown; `packages/cli/src/output/fixReport.ts#DEFER_REASON_LABELS` then renders it as “checkout missing” or “detached HEAD”. Narrow the handling to the expected git exit status (detached HEAD is `symbolic-ref -q` exit 1), rethrow or surface unexpected failures, and add a timeout/non-detached-failure test.

findings.title: Fix-mode unit fixtures no longer exercise routed findings
findings.description: `findingsResult` at `packages/cli/tests/commands/check.test.ts:72-97` has `fixable: true` with no `fixAction`, and `fixResult` at `packages/cli/tests/commands/check.test.ts:99-106` lacks the now-required `deferred` and `commits` fields declared in `packages/core/src/introspection/types.ts:330-337`. Real routing in `planRoutedFixes` only keeps findings matching `f.fixable && f.fixAction`, so these CLI tests call `mockApplyFixes` with an empty routed subset while the mock still returns `fixed: 1`; a regression that drops every real fixable finding would still pass. `packages/mcp-server/tests/workflowTools.test.ts#MOCK_CHECK_RESULT` uses the same incomplete shape. Add a valid `fixAction` with `subjectIndex`, update mocked `ConsistencyFixResult` objects to include `deferred: []` and `commits: []`, and assert the routed subset passed to `applyFixes`.
